artifact.snippet: Narrative Questions: Each question will include: Question text (story/scenario), Two answer options (A and B), Mapping for each option to its impact on ideological axis scores, Tags for demographic relevance (e.g., #homeowner, #parent).

Provides the array of ideological axes that narrative questions will map to.

constraint.description: All data structures and logic must be implemented in TypeScript.
Narrative questions should be stored in a TypeScript file (e.g., `src/lib/narrative/questions.ts`) as an exported array of objects.
The `NarrativeQuestion` data structure must include a mechanism to map each answer option to changes in ideological axis scores, referencing the `NarrativeAnswerImpact` interface.
New files for narrative questions (types and data) should be placed in `src/lib/narrative/`.

interface.name: NarrativeQuestion
interface.reason: New interface required to define the structure of narrative questions, including ideological impacts and demographic tags.

interface.name: NarrativeAnswerImpact
interface.reason: Existing interface that defines how an answer affects an ideological axis score. This will be used in the `NarrativeAnswerOption` interface.

tests.standards: Unit tests should be written using Vitest. Test files should be co-located with the modules they test, following the pattern `*.test.ts`. Focus on validating the data schema and the correctness of the ideological impact mappings.

ideas.idea: Write a unit test to validate the schema of the `NarrativeQuestion` objects, ensuring all required properties are present and correctly typed.
Write a unit test to verify that the `impacts` array in each answer option correctly references valid `axis_id`s from `ideologicalAxes.ts` and that the `delta` values are within a reasonable range.
Write a unit test to ensure that each sample `NarrativeQuestion` has at least one demographic tag.
